title: Kingsman: The Secret Service
edition: Matthew Vaughn’s 2014 production, UK 2D cinema release classified in December 2014 and released in 2015. UK violence edits apply.
synopsis: Eggsy competes for a place in a private intelligence service. When a billionaire uses free SIM cards to turn strangers against one another, passing the entrance exam becomes the least important test he faces.
verdictRationale: Eggsy risks losing his place by refusing to shoot the dog he raised. That quiet refusal shows a capacity for mercy that his examiners overlook. The church massacre and the musical spectacle of exploding heads, however, repeatedly make violent deaths the payoff to a joke. The ending extends that attitude to a woman offered as a sexual reward.
ageRationale: An extended massacre takes place among ordinary people in a church. Bloody injury, strong swearing and a sexual bargain remain in the UK cinema version even after reductions to violence.
reflection: Eggsy believes that obeying might cost another creature its life. He chooses to lose the post instead. A family can ask when a person in authority deserves obedience and when conscience demands the courage to disappoint them.

themes.name: Mercy toward the vulnerable
themes.evidence: Eggsy refuses the order to kill his dog despite believing it will cost him selection. One decision reveals his priorities.

themes.evidence: Offering his mother and sister a safe home is a concrete good in the closing sequence.

themes.name: Violence as spectacle
themes.evidence: Mass killing is the villain’s plan, yet the church fight and explosive deaths are staged as major attractions.

title: Kingsman: The Golden Circle
edition: Matthew Vaughn’s 2017 sequel, UK 2D feature, BBFC-listed UK home-entertainment version.
synopsis: Eggsy and Merlin survive an attack on Kingsman and discover an American partner agency. To save the people poisoned by Poppy’s drug supply, they must face opponents who would gladly let the victims die.
verdictRationale: Merlin takes Eggsy’s place on a mine. The rescue also includes people the president considers expendable. Both choices affirm the worth of a life. Yet the heroes obtain information through sexual deception, and even dispatching an opponent in a meat grinder becomes a payoff for the audience. The film’s treatment of people as instruments repeatedly undercuts its rescue story.
ageRationale: Intimate contact is used to plant a tracker without the woman’s knowledge. Graphic killing, a cannibalism gag and prolonged danger from poisoned drugs accompany that violation.
reflection: The president decides that people who took drugs deserve abandonment. Merlin gives his own life to keep a rescue possible. Consider the difference between condemning a harmful choice and deciding who still deserves medical care.

themes.name: Self-sacrifice
themes.evidence: Merlin switches places with Eggsy on the mine, giving up his own escape so the mission can continue.

themes.name: Care for people in danger
themes.evidence: Getting the antidote to all the poisoned people is the central objective, even when officials prefer to let them die.

themes.name: Sexual exploitation
themes.evidence: A covert tracker is planted during intimate contact. The strain on Eggsy’s relationship receives more attention than the target’s consent.

themes.name: Cruelty as comedy
themes.evidence: A meat grinder and cannibalism furnish recurring grotesque jokes across opposing sides of the conflict.

title: The King's Man
edition: Matthew Vaughn’s 2021 live-action First World War prequel, 2D feature.
synopsis: Orlando Oxford tries to shield his son Conrad from the war as their household uncovers a conspiracy. Conrad enlists under another name and encounters a wounded man carrying intelligence across the front.
verdictRationale: Conrad’s bravest act is carrying a wounded man who cannot make his own way back. His death at the hands of his own side gives Orlando’s fears real weight. The film’s gentleness toward the grieving father sits uneasily alongside the use of Conrad as sexual bait and a finale that settles the conflict by killing the Shepherd.
ageRationale: Bloody trench combat, a sudden fatal shooting by a fellow soldier and graphic wounds give the war scenes lasting weight. The Rasputin episode adds prolonged sexual innuendo and invasive physical contact.
reflection: Conrad’s borrowed name complicates his claim to glory. On the battlefield he finds a simpler obligation in a man who needs carrying. His father learns what his son did only after losing the chance to speak to him.

themes.name: Care under fire
themes.evidence: Conrad returns under fire with a wounded man, accepting a risk that gives his service its clearest moral purpose.

themes.name: Mutual service
themes.evidence: Polly and Shola help sustain Orlando after his loss and play decisive roles in resolving the conspiracy.

themes.name: Wartime brutality
themes.evidence: Trench fighting and Conrad’s sudden death expose the cost of war, alongside choreographed combat presented as adventure.

themes.name: Abuse of spiritual authority
themes.evidence: Rasputin secretly poisons a child, then uses his apparent power over the child’s recovery to pressure the parents.

themes.evidence: Polly proposes using Conrad as bait based on Rasputin’s reported interest in young men. The dinner includes suggestive dialogue and Rasputin treats Orlando’s wound in a sexualized sequence. Check the full episode and the remainder for a rubric-level prominence estimate.
